approach: Add an incremental runner in athena-gate attribution.rs on top of the existing `walk`. `run_check(git, main_tip, now, &Options)` picks a mode. Incremental mode reads the newest checkpoint (by records-branch order) from `checkpoints/`, and walks only main commits after `checkpoint.main_sha`. It judges only records added since `checkpoint.records_sha`, using a new range audit `audit_history_since` in records_branch.rs. It falls back to a full replay, with a stated reason, when there is no checkpoint, the check version differs, or the checkpoint names a main commit or records tip that is not an ancestor. Full-replay mode ignores checkpoints, judges everything, and fails if a checkpoint names a main commit the replay fails on. After a pass with writing enabled and no pending commit, it writes a Checkpoint record through the records writer. The CLI adds `--full-replay` and `--no-checkpoint` to `check --attribution`, and treats env `CI` as read-only. It also checkpoints after a landed `athena land`, and prints seconds, commits judged and records judged. CI runs `check --attribution` on push and `--full-replay` on schedule. Timing comes from a ~200-landing synthetic fixture test that prints both numbers. The CHANGELOG and design doc are updated.

decisions.choice: Put the mode logic, checkpoint read and write, and counters in one `run_check` in athena-gate, reusing `walk` with a start commit and a records-delta parameter. The CLI is a thin caller.
decisions.reason: The logic is testable with the existing gate testutil (`repo`, `commit`, `write`) and without a binary or the host. One function serves `check` and `land`, so criteria 1-7 are tested at the unit level.

rejected.option: Implement the logic in the CLI
rejected.why: It could only be tested through the binary, and `land` needs a real `gh`.

rejected.option: A second walker for incremental mode
rejected.why: Two judging rules could drift. A start/delta parameter on `walk` keeps one rule.

decisions.choice: The newest checkpoint is the one added by the newest records commit on the first-parent chain that touches `checkpoints/`. A helper in records_branch.rs finds it. Record ids and created_at are not used.
decisions.reason: The reading says to choose by records-branch order. A forged `created_at` or id cannot then outrank a real later checkpoint.

rejected.why: Both are writer-supplied data that a tamperer controls.

decisions.choice: Records judged in incremental mode are the landing, intent and bad-record files added since `records_sha` (diff of the two trees). If a new commit has no named landing in that set, widen once: load all intents and landings, and count them as judged.
decisions.reason: A commit after a pending one may have its landing written before the checkpoint. Widening keeps the check sound, and the common case keeps counts equal to the new records.

rejected.why: It would report a false unattributed finding for a landing recorded before the checkpoint.
It defeats the purpose of cost independent of history size (§9).

decisions.choice: Never write a checkpoint when the run has findings, has any pending commit, or is read-only. Read-only is `--no-checkpoint` or env `CI` non-empty, and the CLI computes it once. The workflow keeps `permissions: contents: read`.
decisions.reason: The reading says no checkpoint is written past a pending commit. `main_sha` is the last commit judged before the first pending one, or the tip if none. CI read-only is enforced both by the token and by code.

rejected.option: Detect CI only by the token failing
rejected.why: A failed push is not a mechanism, and a local write would already have moved the branch.

decisions.choice: The checkpoint is written with `RecordsWriter::append_to_remote("origin", ...)` when an `origin` remote exists, and with local `append` otherwise (tests). The id is `RecordId::from_parts(now, bits)`, at `checkpoints/<id>.json`. `verifier_version` is `CHECK_VERSION`, a const built from the crate version plus a rule revision. `Options` carries the version so a test can change it.
decisions.reason: CI reads the checkpoint from the fetched remote branch, so a local-only write would never reach it. Landing already publishes this way.

decisions.choice: Full replay fails on disagreement as follows. It judges everything from the start. If any checkpoint exists whose `main_sha` is not on main's line, or sits at or after a finding, or whose records_sha is not an ancestor of the tip, it adds a `CheckpointDisagrees` finding. A passing replay also writes no checkpoint when read-only.
decisions.reason: This catches a tampered checkpoint that names a commit the replay fails (criterion 2) and keeps the replay exit code 2.

rejected.option: Only compare against the newest checkpoint's sha
rejected.why: The reading names the newest checkpoint, and that is what the replay compares. Checking older ones would not bound trust any better, so only the newest is compared.

decisions.choice: Print the run statistics from main.rs and add them to the JSON there. display.rs is not changed.
decisions.reason: display.rs is not a listed deliverable. The CLI can append the line `attribution run: mode=<incremental|full replay> (reason), <s> seconds, <n> commits judged, <m> records judged`.

decisions.choice: For `land`, a helper in main.rs runs `run_check` incrementally with writing enabled, after `land_pr` returns with `LinkState::Landed`. It is skipped under CI. The helper is unit-tested with a local fixture.
decisions.reason: A landing record already exists when `land_pr` returns Landed. `land_pr` needs the host, so the helper is tested directly and the wiring is one call.

rejected.option: Write the checkpoint inside `Athena::land_pr` in athena-core
rejected.why: athena-core is not a listed deliverable.

risks.risk: Incremental judging could pass something a full replay fails, such as a record added before the checkpoint that changes the verdict for a new commit.
risks.mitigation: Widen to all records when a new commit has no named landing in the delta. The weekly and version-change full replay bounds trust. A test compares incremental and full-replay verdicts.

risks.risk: A concurrent writer moves the records tip between judging and writing, so a checkpoint's `records_sha` is stale.
risks.mitigation: `records_sha` is the tip judged against, as the brief says. A later records commit only adds new records, which the next run judges.

risks.risk: The synthetic 200-landing fixture is slow because each record is its own git commit.
risks.mitigation: Use the existing git test helpers, keep one commit per landing, and run it in the normal `cargo test` only if it takes seconds. Otherwise mark it `#[ignore]` and name the command, though the criterion needs it to run.
Print the figures labelled as measured on the fixture. The assertions are on counts only. Never on seconds.

risks.risk: A forged checkpoint naming a good-looking commit is trusted by the incremental runs.
risks.mitigation: That is the design's accepted bound (§9). The weekly full replay compares against the newest checkpoint.

demonstrations.method: Build a fixture with 3 attributed landings and run a passing check that writes a checkpoint. Add 2 more landings and run again.
demonstrations.observes: The second run is incremental. Commits judged is 2 and records judged equals the files the 2 landings added (intent plus landing each). Both are lower than a full replay's counts.
demonstrations.fails_without: A run that ignores the checkpoint reports all the commits and records, so the equality assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Write a checkpoint record by hand naming an unattributed main commit, whose later commit fails. Run in full-replay mode, then run the CLI test for exit status.
demonstrations.observes: The replay yields a `CheckpointDisagrees` finding and `passed()` is false. `check --attribution --full-replay` exits 2 (binary test in crates/athena-cli/tests/binary.rs).
demonstrations.fails_without: If the replay trusted the checkpoint, it would pass or skip the bad commit.

demonstrations.method: Write a checkpoint with version A. Run with `Options` version B.
demonstrations.observes: The run is a full replay, counts equal the whole history, and the reason text contains both versions and says the check version changed.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the version comparison the run would stay incremental.

demonstrations.method: Build a fixture with an unattributed commit and run with writing enabled. A second case has a pending commit.
demonstrations.observes: The report fails, `checkpoint_written` is None, and the records tip (`resolve_tip`) is the same sha before and after. For the pending case, no checkpoint is written for it either.
demonstrations.fails_without: A writer that is not gated on `passed()` would move the tip.

demonstrations.method: A gate test passes and then reads the new record. A CLI unit test calls the post-landing helper. A binary test runs `athena check --attribution` in a temp repo.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-gate attribution::tests::passing_check_writes_checkpoint && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli checkpoint_after_landing && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test binary check_attribution_writes_checkpoint
demonstrations.observes: The parsed Checkpoint has the last passing main sha, a records_sha equal to the tip judged against, and the CHECK_VERSION. The records tip advanced by exactly one commit.
demonstrations.fails_without: No checkpoint record would exist after a pass.

demonstrations.method: With a valid checkpoint present, run in full-replay mode and compare counts with a fresh no-checkpoint run. Run with writing disabled, and run the binary with env `CI=true`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-gate attribution::tests::full_replay_ignores_checkpoints_and_read_only_never_writes && cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test binary check_attribution_in_ci_writes_nothing
demonstrations.observes: Replay counts equal the whole history. No new records commit appears in either read-only case, and the tip is unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: A replay that used the checkpoint would show lower counts. A writer ignoring read-only would move the tip.

demonstrations.method: Run the binary on a fixture, in text and `--json` forms.
demonstrations.observes: The output contains the mode, a seconds figure, `commits judged` and `records judged` with the expected numbers. The JSON has matching keys.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the reporting line, the assertions on the output fail.

demonstrations.method: Generate a repo with 200 landings by a loop of commit, intent and landing writes. Time `run_check` full replay, write a checkpoint, add 1 landing, and time an incremental run. Print both.
demonstrations.observes: stdout shows 'measured on the synthetic 200-landing fixture: full replay X s (N commits, M records); incremental Y s (1 commit, 2 records)'. It asserts the incremental counts are 1 commit and 2 records.

The top-level `permissions: contents: read` is unchanged. A push runs `athena check --attribution`, and the `schedule` event runs `athena check --attribution --full-replay`. No `contents: write` is added.

The entry describes the checkpoint, incremental, full-replay and CI behaviour. It quotes the fixture timings labelled 'measured on the synthetic fixture' and states that the timing on this repository is taken after landing.

demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0 across the workspace.

Does `legacy.rs` construct `AttributionReport` with struct literals? If so, the new `records_judged` field needs updating there, and legacy.rs is not a listed deliverable. I used `Default`, so this is probably fine.
Whether the CI `CI` env var counts as read-only with `athena land` is a judgement. I plan to skip the checkpoint under CI there too.
How a pre-cutover repository without `legacy-exempt` interacts with checkpoints is not covered. The CLI calls `check_attribution`, not the legacy variant, so I kept that path the same.
